cultural.vision_reason: This is a kerfed bentwood box with opercula-shell inlay along the rim, a classic Northwest Coast (Haida) form of household container, even though it lacks formline decoration.

physical.title: box; dish
physical.summary: Kerfed and bentwood box, the sides of one piece of alder, cut, steamed and bent, pegged at the vertical seam, and pegged at the bottom to a thick base of red cedar. The sides are curved, and convex, excavated on the inside to leave a sharp edged flat top, inlaid with opercula, none of which is broken or missing. The base has four deep lines cut around the edge of the underside, to accommodate the pegs, and is excavated on the bottom inside. Unusually there are no formline designs on the box. Most of one edge of the base is broken away; one side has been smashed and crudely repaired, and the vertical pegged side seam is splitting open. The whole shows traces of mould and grease.
